# Data contract

The catalog powers the README galleries and future Image 2.5 website from one
source. Schema version **1** retains the existing English/Chinese consumer
fields; multilingual fields are additive. UTF-8 JSON, two-space indentation.

## Sources and generated files

- `data/prompts/<stable-id>.json`: case text, original wording, localizations, inputs, evidence and dated metrics.
- `data/site.json`: branding, destination, localized categories.
- `data/locales.json`: supported language codes, native names and complete UI messages.
- `README*.md`, `prompts/*.md`, `data/catalog.json`: generated by `npm run build`.

Run Node.js 22+, `npm run build`, then `npm run check`. No runtime packages,
database, paid service or translation API is required to build the repository.

## Language fields

`source.post_language` is the language of the creator's post, while
`prompt.original_language` identifies the actual source prompt. Each is a
canonical BCP 47 code or `null` when unknown. They can differ: a Portuguese post
may link an English prompt. Unknown historical post languages are not inferred
from the English editorial text.

`prompt.original_steps` preserves exact source wording as an ordered string
array. For older editor adaptations where no verbatim source was archived, it
is `null`; the source link and adaptation label remain visible. Non-English
originals are fully supported. `prompt.kind` describes the relationship to the
source (`original`, `adaptation`, `translation`), not the language of every
rendered block. Translation does not create another case or change the ID.

`prompt.preserved_literals`, when present, lists exact image text or variables
that every translation must retain. Validation checks both the source wording
and each locale. A prompt consisting only of replacement poster copy remains
in that original language; translating its surrounding explanation does not
translate the text the image must display.

Existing `title`, `summary`, `prompt.steps`, `inputs` and `notes` retain their
`en` and `zh` fields. Additional language records live in
`localizations[locale]` with `title`, `summary`, `steps`, `inputs`, `notes`,
`source_digest` and `translation_method`. Array lengths must match the source.
The digest covers the translation basis; source changes make old translations
fail validation until reviewed. Translate original prompt steps directly from
the original language; translate editorial metadata from its authored English.

The generated catalog projects every supported locale into the existing text
objects. `zh` remains a compatibility alias for `zh-CN`; it is not another
maintained translation. Consumers can use:

```js
const text = entry.prompt.steps[0][locale]; // en, zh-CN, ja, etc.
const legacyChinese = entry.prompt.steps[0].zh; // preserved
const exactSource = entry.prompt.original_steps;
```

The configured locales are English, simplified/traditional Chinese, Japanese,
Korean, French, German, Spanish and Brazilian Portuguese. Adding a language
requires its locale record, UI messages, category labels and complete case
translations; the renderer contains no per-language page templates.

## Evidence and discovery

Keep `model.family`, `variant`, `evidence_url` and `evidence` separate from
`verification.independently_tested` and `test_url`. A source claim is not an
independent generation test. Every image includes its external URL, creator
credit, original post URL and `source-result` kind. Required references and
external processing tools live in `inputs`; an input note is not an image count.

Engagement fields are nonnegative integers or `null`: likes, bookmarks,
reposts, replies and views. Preserve `observed_at`, the exact measured showcase
`source_url` and the observation method. Do not copy a quoted post's numbers.
Each card displays its own source-check and metric dates. Catalog
`source_checked_through` is the latest check date, not proof that all rows were
rechecked that day.

Distinct illustrated recipes from one article use `source.section` to identify
their context. Their individual metrics remain `null` when the platform only
exposes article-wide totals; shared engagement is not multiplied across cases.

`discovery_score` is computed at build time. See [curation](CURATION.md) for the
weights and unknown-value handling. It is not a quality or conversion score.

## Links and website integration

Each localized README is a complete gallery with `case-<id>` anchors. Language
switching targets the same case's image. `prompts/<id>.md` remains a compatibility
landing page, including its existing Chinese anchor.

Import the generated catalog from a recorded commit or explicitly labeled local
snapshot. Cache it with the website build; do not make production requests depend
on GitHub raw. Keep stable IDs and image/source attribution. The website link
currently opens the homepage; it does not promise prompt prefill, generation,
GIF export, or a deployed prompt detail route.
